Needs changes before merge.

This is a SAFETY-tier review. The PR changes posted G-code and the shared work-offset bound. This is the first review.

I read the complete eight-file diff against current upstream `AGENTS.md`. The local trial merge uses main `9b141e1122fad4aca12e6502dd5f4963209b4e68`. The merge commit is `af6bd2ff6751373f8fe496852dee411436bfb209`. Its first parent is the PR head.

**Requested before merge**

1. **Keep control compensation in the XY plane.** `assets/posts/tormach.cps:1167` consumes the compensation request without restoring G17. A valid XZ arc followed by a compensated XY contour posts these blocks with no warning:

   ```gcode
   G18 G2 X-4 Y0 Z-2 I2 K0 F500
   G1 G42 X0 Y0 Z-2 D2 F500
   ```

   Compensation then acts in XZ instead of XY. This can cut the wrong surface. The second probe engages G42 first. It then posts `G18 G2 X40 Y40 Z-2 I2 K0 F500`, also with no warning. `assets/posts/tormach.cps:1177` checks a pending compensation word, but does not check active compensation. Restore G17 before engagement. Refuse a switch to G18 or G19 while compensation is active. Add Tormach to the compensation-plane tests. The same probe inputs produce compensation refusal warnings with main's script.

2. **Do not emit unsupported G74.** `assets/posts/tormach.cps:1365` selects G74 for a reverse tap. Tormach's current [PathPilot post guidelines](https://knowledgebase.tormach.com/770mx/pathpilot-post-processor-guidelines) explicitly list G74 left-hand tapping as unsupported. Use a documented PathPilot operation, or refuse this request by name. Correct the test and the decision record. The extended offset mapping itself agrees with the [770MX programming reference](https://knowledgebase.tormach.com/770mx/programming-770mx).

3. **Update the existing capability contracts.** Four suites fail because they still require Tormach to refuse these requests:

   - `crates/post/tests/comp.rs:195`: `every_other_shipped_post_refuses_control_compensation_by_name`.
   - `crates/app/tests/control_comp.rs:214`: `the_lathe_and_the_other_mill_posts_refuse_a_control_op_by_name_and_the_gate_blocks`.
   - `crates/app/tests/cutter_hand.rs:127` and `:274`: `creation_refuses_a_left_hand_cutter_by_name_on_every_m3_only_post` and `an_edit_to_left_hand_refuses_generation_and_post_until_the_operation_asks`.
   - `crates/app/tests/wear_comp.rs:165`: `the_other_posts_refuse_wear_by_name_and_the_gate_blocks`.

   All four suites pass on bare main. Update Tormach's expected behavior and add it to the supported-post checks. Keep the refusal checks for the other posts.

4. **Resolve the catalog test failures.** `crates/app/tests/example_catalog/support.rs:311` rejects `catalog_3d_rough_finish::rebuilds` and `catalog_3d_rough_finish::regenerates`. Both exceed 60 seconds in the quick gate. Both fail again in a separate run on the trial merge. The same full suite passes on bare main; these cases take 44.257 and 45.707 seconds there. [Issue #3975](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/3975) tracks intermittent budget failures. I did not reproduce a red baseline here, so this result remains blocking under the review instructions. Make the final head pass, or provide a matching failure on bare main.

   ```text
   3d/rough-finish rebuilds: did not finish within 60s; move this case to app heavy: example_catalog or reduce its model
   3d/rough-finish regenerates: did not finish within 60s; move this case to app heavy: example_catalog or reduce its model
   ```

5. **Add the requested extended-offset golden.** `crates/post/tests/tormach_post.rs:33` checks output fragments. The PR adds no recorded NC output for an extended offset. The done criteria of [#4228](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/4228) require a golden test for one. Add the NC golden and name it in the PR body. Pin the actual G40 cancel block too; the present `contains("G40")` check also matches the preamble.

6. **Explain the new test binary.** `crates/post/tests/tormach_post.rs:1` adds a top-level integration binary. Upstream's “New tests join a directory suite” rule requires a one-line reason in the PR body. That reason is absent. Put these tests in an existing domain suite, or add the required reason.

**Local results**

- Both selected debug builds pass: `camcraft-post` and `camcraft-app`.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 113 steps, 108 pass, five fail, no stalls. The test totals are 1,229 passed, seven failed, four ignored.

- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: pass.

**Mutations and direct probes**

I ran two independent mutations on script copies in `/tmp`. The checks use the post CLI built from the trial merge.

| Replace reverse `M4` emission with `M3` | GREEN | RED; detected |

The reverse check also pins the following operation's M3 reset. The offset check pins `G54.1 P500`. A full comparison of the right-hand tap program is byte-identical to main's output. Both plane probes above produce no warning on the PR.

**Goldens moved:** none. The PR changes no existing `.nc`, `.cl`, catalog output or UI snapshot. There are no moved golden lines to inspect. The missing new offset golden is finding 5.

**Optional, non-blocking**

`docs/decisions/4228-tormach-g54-1-p-m4-g74.md:5` and its cost section say `MAX_BOUND` becomes 500. The implementation sets 1000. Update the record to state the chosen bound.

**Previous findings checked first**

| Earlier finding | Result on this head |
|---|---|
| Compensation plane safety | Not fixed. Both direct probes still produce unsafe output without a warning. See blocker 1. |

| Four capability contract suites fail | Partly fixed. `control_comp` and `cutter_hand` pass. `comp` and `wear_comp` still fail. See blocker 3. |

| Missing extended-offset golden and weak G40 assertion | Not fixed. Kept non-blocking, as NeoTech's subsequent review classified the golden request. See the follow-up below. |
| Missing reason for the new test binary | Fixed in the PR body. |

**Requested before merge**

1. **Keep compensation in the XY plane.** `assets/posts/tormach.cps:1167` consumes the pending compensation word without restoring G17. A valid XZ arc followed by a compensated XY contour produces:

   ```gcode
   G18 G2 X-4 Y0 Z-2 I2 K0 F500
   G1 G42 X0 Y0 Z-2 D2 F500
   ```

   No warning is emitted. G18 is still active when G42 engages. The control can compensate in the wrong plane.
   A second valid probe engages G42 first, then emits `G18 G2 X40 Y40 Z-2 I2 K0 F500`, also without a warning.
   `assets/posts/tormach.cps:1177` checks a pending compensation word, but does not guard active compensation.
   Restore G17 before compensation engagement or cancellation. Refuse G18 and G19 arcs while compensation is active.
   Add Tormach to `crates/post/tests/comp_plane.rs` so the guard covers both entry and active compensation.
   These are the same two defects from the earlier local review. Main's script refuses compensation for both inputs.

2. **Refuse an unsupported tapping code.** `assets/posts/tormach.cps:1365` selects G74 for a reverse tap.
   The probe emits `G74 X10 Y20 Z-15 R2 F600` without a warning.
   Tormach's current [PathPilot post guidelines](https://knowledgebase.tormach.com/770mx/pathpilot-post-processor-guidelines) list G74 left-hand tapping as unsupported.
   The issue asks for G74, but this conflicts with the manufacturer's support list.
   Use a documented PathPilot operation, or refuse the request by name. Update the test and decision record.
   This is the earlier G74 finding; the fix commit does not change this code.

3. **Finish the capability contract updates.** These two tests still require the old Tormach refusal:

   - `crates/post/tests/comp.rs:195`: `every_other_shipped_post_refuses_control_compensation_by_name`.
   - `crates/app/tests/wear_comp.rs:165`: `the_other_posts_refuse_wear_by_name_and_the_gate_blocks`.

   The first fails with `tormach must refuse by name: []`.
   The second fails because `posting::post_script` returns `Posted` instead of the expected refusal.
   Both complete suites pass on bare main `e902ee488e2d80cf84267d55898489e10400a073`: post `comp` is 9/9; app `wear_comp` is 5/5. These are PR regressions.
   Update the Tormach support checks for control and wear compensation. Keep the refusal checks for the other posts.
   These failures were part of the earlier local review's capability-contract finding.
